laws.summary: Mandates that wage periods (intervals for salary calculation) shall not exceed one month.
laws.details: No wage period fixed by the person responsible for the payment of wages shall exceed one month, ensuring monthly payments are standard.
remedies: Challenge contract terms enforcing quarterly or semi-annual salary payouts.
Demand monthly accounting ledger updates from payroll.
File claims for interest on delayed monthly wage clearances.

laws.act: Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936
laws.scope: Deductions which may be made from Wages
laws.summary: Restricts salary deductions to statutory fines, absence from duty, or housing benefits.
laws.details: Lists permissible salary deductions: fines, deductions for absence from duty, damage to property, or housing accommodation. All other deductions are illegal and punishable.
remedies: File complaints for arbitrary deductions labeled as 'administrative cuts'.
Check pay slips to ensure deductions align with section 7 classifications.
Demand recovery of cash amounts deducted without written warnings.

laws.act: Section 18 of the Shops and Establishments Act (State-specific)
laws.summary: Entitles employees to receive double the normal wage rate for overtime hours worked.
laws.details: Where an employee is required to work in excess of the normal hours of work (usually 8 or 9 hours a day), he shall be entitled to wages at twice the ordinary rate of wages in respect of overtime.
remedies: Log daily timesheet punch entries and email trails.
Demand overtime calculation charts during payroll disputes.
File overtime non-payment complaints to the local Shop Inspector.

laws.act: Section 28 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872
laws.scope: Agreements in Restraint of Legal Proceedings Void
laws.summary: Invalidates employment contract clauses that block employees from suing the company.
laws.details: Declares that every agreement by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, is void.
remedies: Dispute arbitration-only clauses that block Labor Court access.
Challenge one-sided liability agreements signed under duress.
Consult legal counsel to bypass illegal contract restraints.

laws.act: Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.summary: Grants daughters equal coparcenary (birthright) shares in ancestral properties on par with sons.
laws.details: Reformed by the 2005 Amendment. The daughter of a coparcener shall by birth become a coparcener in her own right in the same manner as the son, and have the same rights in the coparcenary property.
remedies: File partition suits claiming equal property shares as a daughter.
Challenge ancestral property sales executed without your consent.
Submit genealogical tables proving birthright descent.

laws.act: Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.scope: General Rules of Succession in Case of Males
laws.summary: Governs how a deceased male's self-acquired property is shared among Class I heirs (spouse, kids, mother).
laws.details: The property of a male Hindu dying intestate shall devolve: firstly, upon Class I heirs (spouse, mother, son, daughter); secondly, upon Class II heirs if Class I is vacant.
remedies: Obtain a Legal Heir Certificate listing all Class I surviving members.
File claims for equal split of self-acquired bank accounts and plots.
Challenge claims of distant relatives if Class I heirs are alive.

laws.act: Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.scope: Property of Female Hindu to be Her Absolute Property
laws.summary: Declares that any property owned by a female Hindu is her absolute property, ending limited estate rules.
laws.details: Any property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be held by her as absolute owner and not as a limited owner.
remedies: Sell or gift property inherited by you without needing husband/son approval.
File cases to delete family annotations labeling your estate as 'limited'.
Draft Wills disposing of your absolute properties independently.

laws.act: Section 15 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.scope: General Rules of Succession in Case of Female Hindus
laws.summary: Governs devolution of a deceased female's property, prioritizing children, spouse, and husband's heirs.
laws.details: Property of a female Hindu dying intestate shall devolve: firstly, upon sons and daughters (including kids of deceased children) and the husband; secondly, upon heirs of the husband.
remedies: File succession claims for deceased mother's property.
Verify if maternal properties originate from parents or husband (different rules apply).
Object to claims of mother's siblings if husband/children are surviving.

laws.act: Section 21 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.scope: Presumption in Case of Simultaneous Deaths
laws.summary: Presumes that the younger individual survived the elder when deaths occur simultaneously (e.g. in accidents).
laws.details: Where two persons have died in circumstances rendering it uncertain which of them survived the other, it shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, that the younger survived the elder.
remedies: Submit joint death reports and medical certificates showing times of event.
Calculate property devolution assuming the younger child inherited from the father.
Structure probate petitions accordingly.

laws.act: Section 22 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.summary: Grants Class I heirs the first right to buy out another co-heir's share in a business/plot.
laws.details: Where an interest in any immovable property or business of an intestate devolves upon two or more Class I heirs, and one proposes to transfer their interest, the other co-heirs have a preferential right to acquire it.
remedies: Serve written notices exercising your preferential right to buy out a sibling's share.
File court suits to stop external third-party sales of shared family businesses.
Obtain valuation certifications to determine fair buy-out prices.

laws.act: Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925
laws.summary: Mandates that every Will must be in writing, signed by testator, and attested by 2 witnesses.
laws.details: Every testator shall sign or affix his mark to the Will, and the Will shall be attested by two or more witnesses, each of whom has seen the testator sign or received acknowledgment.
remedies: Ensure your Will is signed by at least two independent, non-beneficiary witnesses.
Include a medical fitness certificate from a doctor confirming sound state of mind.
Register the Will at the Sub-Registrar's office to enhance authenticity.

laws.act: Section 213 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925
laws.summary: Requires obtaining a Probate from court to establish executor rights under a Will in major metro cities.
laws.details: No right as executor or legatee under a Will can be established in any Court of Justice, unless a Court of competent jurisdiction in India has granted probate of the Will.
remedies: Apply for a Probate Petition in the High Court/District Court.
Serve notices to all family heirs to verify if they have objections (caveats).
Publish public notice citations in local newspapers as required by court.

laws.act: Section 370 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925
laws.summary: Authorizes courts to issue succession certificates to recover deceased persons debts/securities.
laws.details: A succession certificate shall not be granted with respect to any debt or security to which a right is required to be established by probate or letters of administration, unless under specific exceptions.
remedies: Apply for a Succession Certificate in civil court for bank FD/shares releases.
Submit schedules of all bank account deposits and mutual fund holdings.
Post safety indemnity bonds if required by banking organizations.

laws.act: Section 57 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925
laws.summary: Restricts probate requirements to Wills made in Kolkata, Chennai, and Mumbai, or relating to land in these cities.
laws.details: Specifies that the provisions of Section 213 (mandatory probate) apply only to Wills executed by Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs, or Jains within the territories of Kolkata, Madras, and Bombay.
remedies: Verify if the deceased’s property location requires a mandatory probate.
Skip expensive probates if the property is located in non-metro regions (Letters of Administration apply instead).
Submit Will directly to banking organizations for claims in non-metro areas.

laws.act: Section 2 of the Indian Partition Act, 1893
laws.scope: Power to Order Sale Instead of Division
laws.summary: Empowers courts to order public sale and cash division if physical division of land is impossible.
laws.details: Whenever in any suit for partition, it appears to the court that by reason of the nature of the property, a division cannot reasonably be made, the court may direct a sale of the property and distribution of proceeds.
remedies: Request court-directed sale if dividing a single home/apartment among 5 siblings is impractical.
Participate in internal family bidding auctions to buy out other shares.
Submit valuation reports by registered engineers to set floor prices.

laws.act: Section 4 of the Indian Partition Act, 1893
laws.summary: Allows family members to buy out shares sold by a co-heir to an outsider.
laws.details: Where a share of a dwelling-house belonging to an undivided family has been transferred to a person who is not a member of such family, the court shall value such share and force sale to a family shareholder who wants to buy it.
remedies: File applications to buy out external buyers attempting to occupy ancestral dwellings.
Prevent stranger entry into shared family compounds.
Request court valuations of the external buyer's share.

laws.act: Section 23 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.scope: Special Provision Respecting Dwelling Houses (Note: Repealed)
laws.summary: Previously restricted female heirs from demanding partition of family dwelling houses until male heirs decided (Note: Repealed).
laws.details: Formerly restricted a female heir's right to demand partition of a dwelling house until male heirs chose to divide it. This section was repealed in 2005, giving female heirs immediate rights to partition.
remedies: File partition suits for shared parental houses at any time.
Reference the 2005 Repeal in court to dismiss claims blocking daughter partition suits.
Inquire about inheritance registries to verify property partition filings.

laws.act: Section 25 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.summary: Disqualifies a person who commits murder from inheriting the victim's property.
laws.details: A person who commits murder or abets the commission of murder shall be disqualified from inheriting the property of the person murdered, or any other property in furtherance of which he committed the murder.
remedies: Submit copies of criminal conviction judgments to disqualify an heir.
File claims routing inheritance to next eligible heirs in succession tables.
Obtain copy of FIR/charge sheets to stay inheritance transfers during pending trials.

laws.act: Section 26 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956
laws.summary: Disqualifies children born after an individual's conversion to another religion from inheriting Hindu relative estates.
laws.details: Where a Hindu has ceased to be a Hindu by conversion, children born to him after conversion shall be disqualified from inheriting the property of any of their Hindu relatives, unless they are Hindus at the time of succession.
remedies: Verify the religion status of descendants during succession claims.
Provide proof of reconversion to Hinduism to restore inheritance claims.
Obtain birth certificates showing dates of birth relative to conversion dates.
